scenes.heading: Animal systems
scenes.sub: Trillions of cells, all doing different jobs
scenes.say: Your body is made of trillions of cells, but they don't all do the same job. Some absorb food, some send chemical messages, and some clean your blood. Let's see how they team up.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Players form lines, lines form a team, the team is part of a club
scenes.science: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form systems
scenes.breaks: Players choose their positions. Cells specialise by switching on only some genes, and most can never swap jobs.
scenes.say: Think of a footy club. Each player is a cell, and each one specialises. Players doing the same job form a line, like a tissue. Lines make a team, like an organ. The whole club is like an organ system. But players choose their positions. Cells specialise by switching on only some of their genes.

scenes.heading: Levels of organisation
points: Tissue: similar cells doing one job
Organ: two or more tissue types
Four tissues: epithelial, connective, nervous, muscle
scenes.say: Cells are organised into tissues, organs, organ systems and then the whole organism. A tissue is a group of similar cells doing one job. An organ is made of two or more tissue types. The four animal tissues are epithelial, connective, nervous and muscle. Remember: Every Cat Needs Milk.

scenes.heading: The digestive system
points: Bile emulsifies fat; lipase digests it
Villi and microvilli give a huge surface area
scenes.say: The digestive system breaks big food molecules into small ones. Chewing and churning are mechanical digestion. Enzymes do chemical digestion. Bile from the liver is not an enzyme. It breaks fat into tiny droplets so lipase can digest it. Bile breaks, lipase takes. The small intestine's villi and microvilli give a huge surface area for absorption.

scenes.heading: How a nephron makes urine
steps: Flush out: secrete some ions and drugs
scenes.say: Each kidney has about a million nephrons. First, filtration: blood pressure in the glomerulus pushes water and small molecules into Bowman's capsule. Next, selective reabsorption: all the glucose and amino acids, and most water and salt, go back into the blood. Then secretion moves some ions and drugs into the tubule. What's left is urine. Filter, fetch back, flush out.

scenes.heading: Excretion vs egestion
scenes.say: Don't mix up excretion and egestion. Excretion removes wastes your body made, like urea. Egestion removes food you ate but never absorbed, as faeces. Urea is made in the liver when extra amino acids are broken down, then the kidneys excrete it. Liver makes, kidney takes.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A gallstone blocks the duct carrying bile to the small intestine. Predict the effect on digestion.
lines: Bile emulsifies fat; it does not digest it
Fat stays as big droplets, small surface area
Answer: less fat absorbed, more fat in faeces
scenes.say: Here's an example. A gallstone blocks the bile duct. What happens? Without bile, fat stays in big droplets with a small surface area. Lipase can only work on the surface, so fat digestion slows right down. Less fat is absorbed, and more ends up in the faeces. Carbohydrate and protein digestion are mostly fine.

points: Bile emulsifies fat; lipase digests it
Hormones only affect target cells with receptors
The blood links all the systems
scenes.say: Quick recap. Specialised cells build tissues, organs and systems. Bile emulsifies fat and lipase digests it. Hormones travel in the blood but only affect target cells with matching receptors. Nephrons filter, reabsorb and secrete. And the blood links every system together. Now try the practice questions!
